subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose a current-session `resetSession(reason?)` capability specifically to successful after-compaction hooks?
rationale: This adds a public plugin capability that can archive active session state and requires a permanent policy for eligible compaction paths, locked sessions, reset failures, and caller ownership.

options.title: Approve the narrow hook contract
options.body: Keep the API limited to successful after-compaction contexts, require lifecycle-owned deferred execution, fix all post-reset persistence paths, and document the contract.

options.title: Keep reset ownership internal
options.body: Remove the public hook API and implement any required compaction recovery through owner-specific internal lifecycle policy instead.

options.title: Pause the core capability
options.body: Close or defer the PR until a narrower plugin API or owner-sponsored compaction recovery design is agreed.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow hook contract
recommendation.body: Keep the API limited to successful after-compaction contexts, require lifecycle-owned deferred execution, fix all post-reset persistence paths, and document the contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The compaction hook lifecycle history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the plugin contract decision.
